title: Repeating patterns: find the smallest unit

sources.name: NCETM — Pattern: identifying the unit of repeat

practice: Try a few problems at your own pace, then return to any explanation you want to revisit.

sections.title: What is the unit of repeat?
sections.html:
The unit of repeat is the smallest block that can be repeated to make the whole pattern. In circle, square, circle, square… it is circle–square. Four shapes would work too, but they would not be the smallest block.

Think of a striped scarf: you want the little sequence the knitter keeps using, not a description of the entire scarf.

sections.title: Find the minimum period
sections.html:
The period is the number of positions before the pattern repeats. For ABABAB, the minimum period is 2: A alone fails, but AB works all the way along.

Now try AABAABAAB. A fails. AA fails at the third position. AAB works: the minimum period is 3, even though there are only two different letters.

Start with a short candidate block, repeat it and compare every position. If one position disagrees, that block does not describe the full example. The NCETM guide to patterns explains why finding the smallest unit matters more than naming every item.

sections.title: Two circles in a row are not always a mistake
sections.html:
Try the unit circle–square–circle. Repeat it and you get circle–square–circle | circle–square–circle. Two circles meet at the join. Looking only at that pair could send you down the wrong path.

A short sequence can also fit several rules. These examples explicitly ask for a repeating rule; they are not proof that any short list has only one possible continuation.

sections.title: What comes after ABBABBAB?
sections.html:
B, if the rule is to repeat ABB. Group it as ABB | ABB | AB: the final group is missing its last B. The visible sequence does not need to end at a complete block.

A pattern that grows, such as 2, 4, 6, 8, needs a different explanation. Next, try checking every step in a number pattern, or put your eye for patterns to work in the Reasoning Challenge.

description: Find the shortest part that repeats in a pattern. Simple examples explain the unit of repeat, the minimum period and how to check what comes next.
